gaps.sentence: All ___ I want is a quiet weekend at home.
gaps.explanation: After 'all' the relative pronoun is 'that' (often omitted); 'all what' is always wrong.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ produces these parts has factories in three countries.
gaps.explanation: A company takes 'which' as subject; 'who' is normally reserved for individual people.

gaps.sentence: Have you met the couple ___ son is in your class?
gaps.hint: the son belongs to the couple
gaps.explanation: 'Whose son' means 'their son'; the possessive relative 'whose' is required.

gaps.sentence: He showed me the drawer in ___ the keys were kept.
gaps.explanation: 'In which' is the formal relative pattern for things; 'in where' is ungrammatical.
'What caused the fire' means 'the thing that caused it'; 'that' cannot act as the subject of this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.

gaps.sentence: Show me ___ you have written so far.
gaps.explanation: 'What you have written' means 'the things that you have written'; 'that' cannot head a nominal clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.
